title: Add conformance tests for selector v2 kernel candidates across seq buckets
author: Anika Gupta
description: Context: Kernel auto-selection v2 increases the number of attention/prefill/decode kernels we may select based on model family + seq regime + GPU SKU. We’ve seen (a) rare NaN/overflow issues under specific shapes and (b) occasional shape/layout mismatches when a kernel is invoked outside its supported envelope. This PR adds a conformance/correctness test suite that exercises the kernel candidates we intend to ship (the “safe kernel set”) across representative shapes and the same seq-length buckets the selector uses (prefill vs decode, with short/med/long context). What’s included: A new GPU conformance harness that runs reference attention (baseline kernel) and the candidate kernel on identical inputs and compares outputs within tolerance; explicit NaN/Inf guards; deterministic seeding; and per-kernel capability gating (skip with reason when a kernel doesn’t support a shape instead of silently passing). The suite covers common architectures/flags we care about for v2 selection (MHA and GQA; fp16/bf16; typical head dims; cache lengths spanning the buckets). How it’s wired: Tests run on the CUDA GPU CI lane (sm80 runner) and are shardable; the matrix is intentionally limited to keep runtime reasonable while still catching the class of issues we saw in canary. This should reduce risk of shipping a selector table entry that is “fast but wrong” for a bucket. Notes: This PR does not change kernel selection logic; it only adds tests and small helper utilities used by the test harness. Follow-ups are tracked in ENG-3928 for expanding GPU coverage (sm75/sm90) as capacity allows. Checklist: [x] Adds conformance suite covering prefill+decode buckets [x] Adds NaN/Inf guards and clear failure messages [x] Adds docs for running locally on a GPU devbox [x] Keeps CI runtime < ~12m on the GPU lane
commits: test(runtime): add kernel conformance harness w/ reference runner
test(runtime): add representative shape + seq-bucket matrix (prefill/decode)
test(runtime): add NaN/Inf guards + tighter error reporting
docs(runtime): document how to run conformance tests locally and in CI
ci: shard conformance tests on gpu runners
testing: CI: runtime_unit_tests (pass), runtime_gpu_tests_sm80 (pass), lint (pass). Local: ran `tools/dev/run_gpu_conformance_tests.sh --focus attention --shard 0/2` on A100 80GB; verified failures reproduce deterministically when injecting a known-bad kernel (manual sanity check).
review_conversation: Grace Kim (review): Can we make sure the seq buckets match selector v2 exactly (boundaries + prefill/decode split) so we don’t diverge over time? Also please add a failure message that prints (kernel_id, dtype, head_dim, n_heads, n_kv_heads, q_len, kv_len).

Anika Gupta (author): Yep—updated to import the bucket definitions from the same module used by selector context (no re-declared constants). Also added a structured failure header with the full shape context + bucket name; see `format_failure_context()` in `kernel_runner.py`.

Yuki Sato (review): GPU lane is sm80-only. Can we at least ensure the tests don’t assume A100-specific behavior (e.g., bf16 availability)? Also the capability gating: prefer explicit “unsupported on sm80” vs broad skip so we notice if we’re unintentionally skipping most cases.

Anika Gupta (author): Good call. I made bf16 cases conditional on `device_supports_bf16()` and the skip reasons are now explicit: (unsupported dtype, unsupported head_dim, unsupported layout, unsupported sm). The summary prints a skip histogram at the end of the run so we can spot over-skipping.

Hiro Tanaka (review): Output tolerance: I’m nervous about too-loose thresholds masking real issues. Can we tighten for fp16/bf16 and only widen for known numerically unstable combos? Also please add an explicit NaN/Inf assertion before comparing.

Anika Gupta (author): Tightened default tolerances (fp16: atol=2e-2/rtol=2e-2; bf16: atol=3e-2/rtol=3e-2) and added per-kernel override hooks. Added NaN/Inf checks on both reference and candidate outputs before computing diffs; failures now say whether NaNs came from reference or candidate.

Omar El-Sayed (review): Can you wire this so it can run targeted against the “safe kernel set” rather than hardcoding kernel IDs in the test? We’ll be updating the registry and I don’t want to keep editing tests.

Anika Gupta (author): Done. Tests enumerate kernel candidates via `runtime/kernels/registry/safe_kernel_set.py` (which is what selector v2 will use for fallback). The test logs the resolved list at runtime to keep it auditable.
Sahana Iyer (review): CI runtime is ~15m on my branch; can we shard by bucket or by kernel id? Also please ensure the test suite is opt-in on non-GPU CI lanes.
Anika Gupta (author): Sharded by (kernel_id, bucket) pairs into 2 shards for now; on sm80 lane it’s ~10–11m. Non-GPU CI skips these tests entirely (guarded by `requires_cuda_gpu`).
merge_outcome: Merged to main; will ship with runtime-1.19 as part of selector v2 hardening.
